text: Co-packaged optics (CPO) is called the commercial 'beachhead' for photonics inside the computer. Roughly what energy-per-bit change does moving from faceplate pluggables into the ASIC package deliver at 51.2 Tb/s switch scale?
choices: From about 5 pJ/bit down to about 1 pJ/bit
No energy improvement; CPO only reduces latency
From about 50 pJ/bit down to about 25 pJ/bit
From about 12 to 15 pJ/bit down to about 5 pJ/bit, roughly halving switch optics power
explanation: Faceplate pluggables run at roughly 12 to 15 pJ/bit; co-packaging the transceiver in the ASIC package drops this to about 5 pJ/bit, roughly halving switch optics power at 51.2 Tb/s and removing the painful electrical trace at 100+ Gb/s per lane. The other options invert or fabricate the figures, and CPO's benefit is energy, not merely latency.
